heading: THE FIELD TEST №19
sub: groundstation · 3 prompts re-run · 1 live artifact · 2 fixed, 0 partly, 1 the same · October 27, 2026 · Development Seed labs
lede: The finish-line run for the MVP. Stops 34 to 37 landed today (PRs 102, 103, 104, 106) and this run asks the same 3 cards as field test 18, in the same words and with the same tool calls, on main at 0.59.0. Each learning opens with its verdict, grounded only in the new raw output: 2 fixed, 0 partly, 1 the same. The one that stayed the same is the Landsat card, where nothing was meant to move.

cases.answer: The 2023 search now returns 1 scene per tile, and the 2023 statistics say in words that their extreme values are not real vegetation. The search over 2023-08-18 to 08-19 comes back with 2 items, one per tile (15SYS covers 41.1% of the box, 15SXS covers 100.0%), both processed 2024-10-26, with folded_duplicates: 2 and a note that 2 older processings of the same scene were dropped. The recommendation reads "clearest (0.0% cloud) and best-covering (100.0% of the area), not a tradeoff". To the digit the 15SYS scene is the clearer one (cloud 0.007472 against the pick's 0.014582), but both print as 0.0%, so the reason holds at the precision it prints (my reading). The 2023 NDVI statistics carry a range_note saying the index ran from -64 to 4.067, that pixels under digital number 1000 go below 0 after the -0.1 offset, that the values are not clamped, and that the median (0.5799) and percentiles (0.1026 and 0.9498) are the safer summary. The mean is 0.5358. The 2021 scene (offset 0, 65.04% cloud scene-wide) has min -0.5272, max 0.7693, and no range_note. Index statistics over a 14 by 11 km box, not damage evidence.
cases.learning: Fixed. Field test 18 searched the same box and window and got 4 items (the no18 card names the one 15SXS id, ...20230819T021410, and the tile 15SYS item and the later-processed copies are not itemized there); now the search returns 2, with ids ending 20241026T035856, and says folded_duplicates: 2. The reason contrasts the pick with no other scene; the no18 card did not quote a reason for this search, so the self-contrast stop 34 removed is not shown in either field test's output. For the statistics, min -63.999999999998195 and max 4.066666666666659 are unchanged from no18, but they now come with a range_note in plain words; the 2021 scene, whose offset is 0 and whose range is -0.5272 to 0.7693, has none. Two things worth saying. First, the statistics call used the older item id ...20230819T021410 so the arguments stay identical to no18; the search no longer returns that id, and the call still worked, returning the same mean, median, std, percentiles and count as no18 to the digit. Second, the 2021 search returned 2 items with no folding key, which fits there being no reprocessed copies (my reading; the output only shows the absence of the key). Not checked: whether the dropped copies differ in content from the kept ones, the apply_scaling=False path, and whether 0.5358 holds against an independent source.

cases.answer: Nothing on this card changed: the same 8 scenes, the same pick (2026-10-05, 15.28% cloud, 100.0% coverage), and the same reason ending with why the newest day, 2026-10-21, lost. The bare name "Portland" is still ambiguous (4 candidates), so I used the Casco Bay box of Portland, Maine, as the earlier cards did. The reason still ends "the newest, 2026-10-21, lost on cloud: 23.0% against the pick's 15.3%, outside the 5-point tie". Asked with limit=3 the search returns 3 scenes and picks the 2026-10-21 scene with no such clause. Neither search carries folded_duplicates or a note, so the Landsat items were not folded.
cases.learning: The same. That is the expected result here, not a gap: stop 34 folds reprocessed copies of one scene, and no 2 of the 8 Landsat ids share a path, row and date, so there was nothing to fold; nothing should change, and nothing did. Count (8 and 3), ids, cloud and coverage figures, the geocode ambiguity note and both reason texts match field test 18 character for character, checked line by line against the no18 cases file; the candidate lines here leave out the type and extent_basis columns no18 printed, so those columns are not compared. The stop 32 newest-scene clause still holds, and is still absent when the pick is the newest day. What this card cannot say: whether the fold would fire on Landsat when duplicates exist (the fold in src/groundstation/tools.py keys the tile on s2:mgrs_tile, else grid:code; whether these Landsat items carry grid:code is not in the output), and the ceiling-step and coverage-step wordings, which no live data here reaches. Not checked: a render of the pick.
cases.shows: stop 34 does not disturb a non-Sentinel collection · no folded_duplicates on Landsat · count 8 and 3, pick and reason as in no18 · stop 32 newest-scene clause still reads as before · geocode ambiguity still lists 4 Portlands

cases.answer: The brief now measures NDVI over the county box, says how much of the county that covers, and says out loud that it cannot tell whether the scenes moved since the last run. The pick is the same scene as field test 18, S2C_10UFU_20261023_0_L2A (cloud 8.8687, 47.6% of the area), and the baseline is the same, S2C_10UFU_20261003_0_L2A. The means are now 0.499 and 0.525, not the whole-tile 0.544 and 0.614 of field test 18, and the metric label reads "NDVI (vegetation) over Chelan County, Washington, 47.6% of it covered". The change is a drop of 0.026 (-4.9%), against -0.07 (-11.5%) before. The brief carries "Since the last run: ..." under What changed and does not say "nothing has changed". The state file now holds both scene ids for the next run.
cases.learning: Fixed. Stop 35: the label names the place and the covered share (47.6%), and both means moved from the whole tile (0.544 and 0.614 in field test 18) to the place's box (0.499 and 0.525); the 2 scenes are the same as field test 18, and both runs are dated 2026-10-26. Stop 37: the stored state from 2026-10-26 had only the mean, and previous_run.scene_vs_last_run reads "the prior run carried no scene ids, so whether the pick or baseline moved is unknown", which is the honest answer, and the brief text repeats it instead of the earlier habit of saying nothing changed (the phrase appears 0 times in the brief html; field test 18's brief, docs/img/ft18-chelan-brief.html, said "Nothing has changed since the 2026-10-25 CALM run"). The caption ("Sentinel-2, 2026-10-23, 8.9% cloud cover, covers 48% of the area") and the map layer ("Sentinel-2 2026-10-23 (8.9% cloud)") still name the one pick, and S2C_10UFU_20261023_0_L2A is the only scene id in the map html; the map image shows that one tile over Lake Chelan. Not checked: the other branch, a prior run that did carry scene ids and either matched or moved (this run could only exercise the no-ids branch; the next run on this place will carry pick_id and baseline_id for it), the share label when the pick covers 99% or more of the place, and the metric label and scene_vs_last_run strings against a committed file: the brief md and data.json were not committed, so those 2 quotes rest on the run's output, though the committed brief html carries the same "Since the last run" sentence.
